reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes Forsage as an online earning platform and instructs viewers to join through a referral link, identify an upliner, connect a wallet, approve BUSD, and complete registration. The flow visibly uses referral and team-oriented structures, including an inviter, upliner, Forsage programs, and priority-leader language, indicating participation tied to a recruitment hierarchy rather than an ordinary wallet tutorial.

opening.argument: The evidence supports a cautious, non-guaranteed presentation rather than a deceptive promise. The description uses promotional praise, but calling a platform “best” is an opinion, not proof of guaranteed profit. The narration explains account setup and wallet steps; it does not state that viewers will earn a particular amount, receive a payout, or avoid loss. The supplied material also does not establish a completed transaction or resulting income. A careful judge should distinguish optimistic marketing language from an explicit guarantee, especially where the content itself primarily gives procedural instructions.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats referral and upliner terminology as conclusive proof of a recruitment scheme. But those words establish only that the registration flow uses an identifier and link; they do not establish guaranteed returns, deceptive claims, or a payout to the creator. The cited “priority” interface is also only a displayed interface element, not proof of what the video promises viewers.

citations.quote: check the ID of upliner register now connect wallet

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a stated payout does not make the promotion safe. The description explicitly presents Forsage as an earning platform, while the instructions direct viewers through a referral link, upliner identification, wallet connection, BUSD approval, and registration. Those steps show an earning opportunity tied to participation and referral structure, even without a numerical guarantee.

opening.argument: The central act shown is an operational walkthrough: the title says “How to register,” and the narration proceeds through opening a wallet, locating a referral link, connecting the wallet, approving BUSD, and logging into the account. The frames likewise show registration and account-preview screens rather than a narrated testimonial of earnings. A tutorial can explain how a third-party application works without independently certifying its profitability or soliciting a particular result. On this record, the strongest characterization is technology and account-navigation instruction.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution describes tutorial steps as if they were themselves a solicitation. Yet the quoted material mainly tells viewers where to click and how to complete registration. The screenshots show application screens, but they do not establish that the presenter personally recruited anyone, promised income, or represented the system as risk-free. Tutorial subject matter should not be converted into a scam finding merely because the application has referral fields.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the video a tutorial does not change what the tutorial teaches. It directs viewers to a referral link and an upliner ID, then instructs them to connect a wallet, approve BUSD, and register. The title identifies the platform and mobile registration, while the earning description supplies the promotional context. The operational format is therefore the means of promoting participation, not neutral technology education.

opening.argument: Even viewed as promotion, the supplied evidence does not establish the core mechanism of a scam. It shows a platform-registration workflow and wallet interaction, but no stated downline commission, guaranteed return, required recruitment quota, or actual payout. The narration says to use a referral link and identify an upliner, yet it never explains that viewers must recruit others for income. The frames show interface fields and account status, not a demonstrated loss or transfer to the presenter. A referral-based online service can be promoted without the record proving fraudulent operation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution infers the missing mechanism from labels such as “upliner” and from a referral link. But inference cannot supply the absent explanation of commissions or required recruitment. A visible account page and registration screen show how the service is accessed, not that participation depends on recruiting a downline or that money is promised. The evidence therefore supports referral registration, while leaving the alleged scam mechanism unproven.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The mechanism is not limited to an explicit sentence promising commissions. The content advertises Forsage as an online earning platform and walks viewers through a referral link and upliner ID before wallet approval and registration. The frames include an account page with a “Join Priority Leaders” element and partner/team-style fields. Together, these features support participation in a tiered recruitment structure even though no individual payout is shown.
